<description>
[quoted text omitted]

This reduces the size of bitcoind by ~`0.5mb`, and bitcoin-qt by `1.3mb` (`aarch64-apple-darwin`).

This option exists for lld, which is why it's only added for darwin builds.
</description>

participants:
  0xB10C (contributor): neutral; provided Guix build hashes
  davidgumberg (contributor): support; ACKed with size benchmark measurements and Guix hashes
  sedited (contributor): neutral; provided Guix build hashes
  Sjors (member): objection; demonstrated that --icf=safe without -faddrsig folds address-significant functions on Darwin
  theuni (member): objection; concerned that Guix-only linker flags would hide linker issues from developers; resolved by moving flags to general build

claims:
  c:4461546707 | Sjors (member) | 2026-05-15 | correctness | open | blocking; author replied in c:4461591584, c:5238854292
    harm: Without -faddrsig, --icf=safe on Mach-O targets behaves like --icf=all, breaking function pointer uniqueness and folding address-significant functions.
    quote: "My LLM friend thinks that `--icf=safe` is not actually safe, because without an address-significance table (`-faddrsig`) it's equivalent to `--icf=all`."
  c:4499825348 | theuni (member) | 2026-05-20 | maintenance | resolved | nonblocking; author replied in c:4875779934; settled by c:4875779934: "I've pulled this back out of REDUCE_EXPORTS, into the general flags."
    harm: Enabling ICF only for Guix builds hides potential linker issues from developers building locally.
    quote: "I worry that if any linker tricks like this cause any trouble, we'd only see it in guix binaries."
  rc:3652466874 | hebasto (member) | 2026-07-26 | approach | open | nonblocking; no author reply
    harm: The linker flag probe order appends --icf=safe after --icf=safe_thunks, which causes safe to override safe_thunks on toolchains supporting both.
    quote: "This prioritizes `--icf=safe` over `--icf=safe_thunks` on the linker command line. However, shouldn't it be the other way around, since `safe_thunks` does not rely on the address-significance table?"
  c:5136916557 | 151henry151 (contributor) | 2026-07-30 | correctness | open | blocking; no author reply
    harm: On the pinned Guix toolchain, LLD 19 Mach-O folds address-taken functions unless -faddrsig is passed across core and depends, corrupting dispatch tables and function identity.
    quote: "Not an ACK in its current shape — on the pinned Guix toolchain, `--icf=safe` behaves like `--icf=all` for the Darwin release binaries. Adding `-faddrsig` fixes that and keeps most of the size win"
support:
  c:4446990079 | davidgumberg (contributor) | 2026-05-14 | ACK | substantive: nice win in binary sizes, with Guix size benchmarks showing ~5% savings across Darwin binaries
  r:4781720529 | hebasto (member) | 2026-07-26 | Concept ACK | substantive: on using the "Identical Code Folding" linker feature where possible.

<previous_assessment>
- open concerns: On Mach-O targets with LLVM 19, -Wl,--icf=safe without -faddrsig folds address-significant functions, breaking C++ function pointer uniqueness invariants (Sjors, 151henry151).
- open concerns: Enabling true safe folding requires adding -faddrsig to Darwin compilation flags across core and depends (151henry151).
- open concerns: Probe order in CMakeLists.txt will cause safe to override safe_thunks on toolchains supporting both (hebasto, 151henry151).
- resolved concerns: Moving the linker probe from REDUCE_EXPORTS into general linker flags (theuni, fanquake).
- davidgumberg ACKed an earlier revision with Guix benchmark data showing ~5% size savings
- Sjors provided a reproducer demonstrating function pointer comparison failures when address-significant folding occurs
- 151henry151 reviewed at 24ad7419de stating 'Not an ACK in its current shape' and showed that adding -faddrsig preserves almost all size savings while preventing incorrect symbol collisions
- hebasto agreed that -faddrsig must be enabled explicitly for macOS targets and noted the probe order issue
</previous_assessment>
